title: 312. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Identifying Inappropriate Extrapolation from Graphs
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate whether extending a linear graph far beyond its observed interval is appropriate.
questions.question: A graph shows a company’s monthly sales from January to June, and the points lie close to a straight line. A student extends this line to December to predict sales. Which evaluation is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: The extrapolation is appropriate because the graph is linear.

options.label: B
options.text: The extrapolation is potentially inappropriate because the trend may change outside the observed interval.

questions.explanation: The graph provides data only from January to June. Extending the line to December goes far beyond the observed interval. Even if the January–June trend is nearly linear, sales may change because of seasonality, market changes, or other factors. Therefore, the extrapolation is potentially inappropriate.
questions.hint: Consider whether the prediction lies inside or outside the interval where data were actually observed.

questions.concept: Extrapolation Outside the Domain of a Graph
questions.learningObjective: Identify why predicting outside the observed time interval may be inappropriate.
questions.question: A graph shows outdoor temperature from 6 AM to 6 PM. A student uses the graph to predict the temperature at midnight by extending the curve. Which evaluation is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The prediction is appropriate because the graph is continuous.

options.label: B
options.text: The prediction is inappropriate because midnight lies outside the observed interval, and the daily temperature cycle may reverse.

questions.explanation: The graph only describes temperature from 6 AM to 6 PM. Predicting midnight requires extrapolation beyond the observed interval. Because temperature typically falls at night, the daytime trend may not continue, so the extrapolation is inappropriate.
questions.hint: Check whether the predicted time is within the interval covered by the graph.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether extending an exponential growth curve far beyond the data is reliable.
questions.question: A graph shows a bacteria population growing exponentially from hour 0 to hour 5. A student extends the curve to predict the population at hour 10. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The extrapolation is inappropriate because exponential growth may not continue indefinitely due to limited resources.

options.label: B
options.text: The extrapolation is appropriate because the exponential model fits all the observed data.

questions.explanation: The observed data cover only hours 0 through 5. Although the population grows exponentially during that interval, resources such as nutrients and space are limited. Extending the exponential curve to hour 10 assumes the same growth pattern continues, which may be unrealistic. Thus, the extrapolation is inappropriate.
questions.hint: Consider whether the growth process can continue at the same rate far beyond the observed data.

questions.learningObjective: Compare the reliability of interpolation within the observed interval with extrapolation beyond it.
questions.question: A graph records a plant’s height each week for 6 weeks. Which prediction is generally more reliable?

options.label: A
options.text: Estimating the height at week 3.5, which lies inside the observed interval.

options.label: B
options.text: Estimating the height at week 20, which lies far beyond the observed interval.

questions.explanation: Interpolation estimates a value inside the interval where data were observed. Here, week 3.5 lies between the recorded weeks. Extrapolation to week 20 goes far beyond the data and assumes the growth pattern continues for many more weeks. Therefore, estimating at week 3.5 is generally more reliable.
questions.hint: Compare whether the prediction lies inside or outside the range of the observed data.

questions.concept: Appropriate Linear Extrapolation Under Constant Rate
questions.learningObjective: Determine when a short linear extrapolation is reasonable from a constant-rate graph.
questions.question: A graph shows the distance traveled by a car moving at a constant speed from \(t=0\) to \(t=4\text{ hours}\). A student predicts the distance at \(t=5\text{ hours}\) by extending the line. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The extension is reasonable if the car continues at the same constant speed.

options.label: B
options.text: The extension is always inappropriate because \(t=5\) lies outside the observed interval.

questions.explanation: The graph shows a constant rate of change, so the distance–time relationship is linear on the observed interval. If the car continues at the same constant speed after \(t=4\), extending the line to \(t=5\) is a reasonable short-term prediction. Extrapolation is not automatically invalid; it depends on whether the underlying condition still holds.
questions.hint: Consider whether the constant-speed condition is likely to remain true just beyond the data.

questions.learningObjective: Identify inappropriate extrapolation when a graph covers only part of a repeating cycle.
questions.question: A graph shows average monthly rainfall from January to June, and the points suggest a decreasing trend. A student extends the trend to predict December rainfall. Which evaluation is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: The extrapolation is appropriate because the trend is decreasing.

options.label: B
options.text: The extrapolation is inappropriate because rainfall often follows seasonal patterns, and the graph covers only half a year.

questions.explanation: The graph gives data only from January to June. Rainfall patterns are often seasonal and may rise again later in the year. Extending the decreasing January–June trend to December ignores possible seasonal reversal and goes far beyond the observed interval, so the extrapolation is inappropriate.
questions.hint: Ask whether the variable may follow a repeating yearly cycle rather than a simple continuing trend.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate whether a short-term upward trend supports a long-term prediction.
questions.question: A graph shows a stock price fluctuating over 10 days, with a recent upward trend. A student extends the recent trend to predict the price after 1 year. Which evaluation is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The prediction is appropriate because the recent trend is upward.

options.label: B
options.text: The prediction is inappropriate because a short-term trend may not represent long-term behavior.

questions.explanation: The graph covers only 10 days and includes fluctuations. A recent upward trend over a short time does not guarantee the same behavior over a full year. Many factors can change the stock price, so extrapolating the short-term trend to 1 year is inappropriate.
questions.hint: Consider the difference between a short observed interval and a very long prediction horizon.

questions.concept: Physical Limits of a Quadratic Model
questions.learningObjective: Identify inappropriate extrapolation beyond the physical domain of a projectile graph.
questions.question: A graph models the height of a ball thrown upward. The graph is valid from \(t=0\) to \(t=5\text{ seconds}\), when the ball hits the ground. A student extends the parabola to predict the height at \(t=8\text{ seconds}\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The extrapolation is inappropriate because after \(t=5\) the physical situation changes; the ball has already landed.

options.label: B
options.text: The extrapolation is appropriate because the quadratic curve continues smoothly after \(t=5\).

questions.explanation: The quadratic model describes the ball’s height only while it is in the air, from \(t=0\) to \(t=5\). After \(t=5\), the ball has already hit the ground, so the original physical conditions no longer apply. Extending the parabola to \(t=8\) is therefore inappropriate.
questions.hint: Check whether the real-world process described by the graph is still valid beyond the observed time.

questions.concept: Extrapolation Far Outside the Data Range
questions.learningObjective: Determine why extrapolating far beyond the observed temperature range may be unreliable.
questions.question: A graph shows ice cream sales versus temperature for temperatures from \(10^\circ\text{C}\) to \(30^\circ\text{C}\), and the relationship appears roughly linear. A student extends the line to predict sales at \(45^\circ\text{C}\). Which evaluation is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: The extrapolation is inappropriate because \(45^\circ\text{C}\) is far outside the observed range, and the relationship may change.

options.label: B
options.text: The extrapolation is appropriate because the linear trend can be extended to any temperature.

questions.explanation: The observed data cover only \(10^\circ\text{C}\) to \(30^\circ\text{C}\). Predicting at \(45^\circ\text{C}\) requires extrapolating far beyond that range. Outside the observed conditions, customer behavior, supply limits, or other factors may change the relationship, so the linear trend cannot be assumed to continue. Thus, the extrapolation is inappropriate.
questions.hint: Compare the predicted input value with the range of inputs actually shown on the graph.

questions.concept: Long-Term Extrapolation from a Short Data Interval
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate the reliability of long-term extrapolation from a limited population graph.
questions.question: A graph shows a city’s population from 2000 to 2020, and the points suggest a steady linear increase. A student extends the line to predict the population in 2100. Which evaluation is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: The extrapolation is inappropriate because predicting 80 years beyond the data assumes the same growth pattern for a very long time.

options.label: B
options.text: The extrapolation is appropriate because the population increased linearly from 2000 to 2020.

questions.explanation: The graph provides data for only 2000 through 2020. Predicting the population in 2100 requires extrapolating 80 years beyond the observed interval. Over such a long period, birth rates, migration, economic conditions, and policies may change, so the linear trend may not continue. Therefore, the extrapolation is inappropriate.
questions.hint: Consider how far the prediction lies beyond the last observed year and whether long-term conditions may change.
